text:
tess: Heads-up: polaris-mini-ptq canary (streaming) is spiking structured-output parse errors ~4.3% over baseline. Seems different from usual trailing-comma failures.

raj: Different how?

tess: Samples show duplicate closing brackets inserted then truncated, e.g. sanitized: 
```
{"op":"create","payload":[{"id":1}]}}
...stream cut...
```

anya: Interesting — extra brace then cutoff. Could be tokenization flipping a low-prob '}' earlier and then another token stops, leaving corruption.

raj: CI-bot, run struct-sanity on 400 canary samples (polaris-mini-ptq) vs 400 float baseline and post quick diffs for punctuation tokens.

ci-bot: Running struct-sanity(400). ETA 90s.

raj: Short-term mitigation idea: add "stream-resume" probe that sends a tiny follow-up resume token request to try to complete truncated streams when punctuation pattern suggests mid-JSON. Flag resumed outputs.

anya: I'd prefer non-invasive repair first (dedupe duplicate punct, close unmatched opens) and surface resumed vs repaired. But resume probe could reduce false negatives for canary. Make it opt-in.

ci-bot: Results: polaris-mini-ptq parse_success=90.7%, resumed_success=2.1%, repaired_success=3.6%, final_failure=3.6%. baseline parse_success=95.4%, repaired_success=0.5%, final_failure=4.1%. Full report: /canary/reports/polaris-mini-ptq/2814000123.json

raj: Looks like two things: 1) PTQ tie flips on punctuation, 2) resumed_probe recovers some but repair helps too.

anya: Action items: (1) run token-align focusing on punctuation/EOS tokens, (2) enable opt-in resume-probe + repair for canary, (3) schedule a tiny PTQ calibration sweep (per-channel vs per-tensor) on the canary dataset.

tess: Hold rollout until parse_success + resumed_success + repaired_success >= baseline parse_success - 0.5%. I'll log follow-ups.
